PullRequest.Title: sessions: Decouple GitHub chat pills from the workspace
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Recorded GitHub issues and pull requests currently fall back to the generic Artifacts/References pill when a session has no workspace or the link belongs to another repository.

- Resolve recorded GitHub artifacts and references independently of workspace metadata.
- Share the resolved references across dedicated chat pills, artifact de-duplication, and PR status polling.
- Preserve repository-discovered associations, stable removal IDs, keyboard opening, and unsupported-link fallback without changing the workspace's primary PR association.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — passed with zero errors.
- 56 focused Electron unit tests — passed, covering workspace-less issues/PRs, cross-repository links, removal, polling, and provider behavior.
- Targeted ESLint and `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.

The aggregate compile task stopped on missing dependencies for an unrelated built-in extension; the client-only compile covering these changes passed.

To verify manually, record an issue or PR in a workspace-less quick chat, or record a link from another repository in a workspace session. It should appear in its dedicated GitHub pill, not the generic Artifacts/References pill, and remain openable and removable.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed source, all-session call path, request counts, one-minute schedulers, and lack of a shared limiter are directly traced. Exact catalog sizes vary, but the artifact API accepts unbounded batches and persists entries, so magnitude uncertainty affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST and GraphQL requests plus one live metadata/CI/review model set per unique recorded pull request
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N unique newly included recorded PRs across unarchived sessions, restoration launches 2N metadata/review REST requests concurrently; each open non-draft PR then adds N CI REST and N review-thread GraphQL requests immediately and every minute. Reference collections coalesce duplicate coordinates across sessions, so the effective cardinality is unique PRs, but no limiter or collection bound caps N.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A large session history can create sustained background network traffic, GitHub API pressure, and request bursts after workbench restore even when none of those sessions or pills is open.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The poller read only getGitHubPullRequestRefs(gitHubInfo), which required a workspace repository; agent-host promotion also kept repository metadata scoped to matching owner/repo, so workspace-less and cross-repository recorded PRs stayed out of global polling.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: getSessionGitHubReferences now adds every recorded PR from session artifacts to each per-session polling identity, including workspace-less and foreign-repository links, and the existing polling loop refreshes and polls every resulting model.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 214 replaces the workspace-scoped getGitHubPullRequestRefs(gitHubInfo) source with getSessionGitHubReferences(session, reader), whose new implementation scans session.artifacts and returns recorded PRs regardless of workspace or repository.
Findings.Title: Bound polling to active or repository-associated pull requests
Findings.Impact: After restore, users with accumulated sessions containing recorded PR links can see a concurrent request burst and continuous background polling. Roughly 20 unique open non-draft recorded PRs already drive about 80 GitHub requests per minute (two PR requests, one CI request, and one GraphQL review-thread request per PR) while VS Code remains open.
Findings.Evidence: GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution initializes trackers from getSessions() at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored and this changed line broadens each tracker to all artifact-derived PRs. _pollPullRequest immediately calls model.refresh(); GitHubPullRequestModel.refresh performs two REST calls in Promise.all. Once an open PR resolves, the same tracker refreshes CI and review-thread models and starts all three schedulers at 60-second intervals. GitHubApiClient issues requests directly through IRequestService with no limiter. parseSessionArtifactInputs accepts an arbitrary non-empty items array, and persisted artifact collections have no size bound.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep all recorded refs available to the pills, but do not enroll every historical ref in catalog-wide one-minute polling. Restrict global polling to repository-associated or active/visible-session PRs, refresh other recorded refs on demand, and use a shared bounded scheduler if background refresh is still required.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restoration and background status polling for unarchived sessions with recorded GitHub pull requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution starts at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored, so polling is off the initial restore critical path, but it begins immediately afterward and remains active for the workbench lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial and repeating GitHub pull-request metadata and review REST requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two immediate requests and two requests per minute for each unique included PR after cross-session model deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only workspace/repository-derived PR references were enrolled; workspace-less and cross-repository recorded links were not polled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background/off restore critical path, but creates sustained traffic and concurrent post-restore bursts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub CI check REST refresh/poll for each resolved open PR
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate request and one request per minute per unique open non-draft PR; drafts poll continuously only while active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No CI model was created for workspace-less or foreign-repository recorded PRs because they did not enter the poller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background, but contributes to aggregate API/network load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub GraphQL review-thread refresh/poll for each resolved open non-draft PR
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate GraphQL request and one per minute per unique open non-draft PR, with no ETag cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace-less and foreign-repository recorded PRs never started review-thread polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background, but adds sustained unconditional network work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N unique owner/repository/PR coordinates among repository associations plus persisted recorded PR artifacts across every unarchived session. Per-session distinct() and shared ReferenceCollections coalesce duplicate coordinates; N unique PRs is the effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Every session tracker iterates its resolved identities synchronously. Unique PR model refreshes launch together without a global limiter; each PR metadata refresh itself uses Promise.all for two REST calls. Shared models coalesce concurrent duplicate-coordinate refreshes and polling clients, but do not bound concurrency across distinct PRs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Duplicate PR coordinates share models. Metadata/review and CI requests retain ETags while models stay referenced, reducing response payloads on warm polls; review-thread GraphQL polling is unconditional. Failures are retried by the next scheduled cycle. Recorded artifacts are persistent and have no collection-size bound.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed source, all-session initialization, model sharing, request multiplicity, one-minute cadence, and absent limiter are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of recorded PRs in typical catalogs is not measured, but artifact batches and persistent collections are unbounded; around 20 unique open non-draft PRs imply roughly 80 requests per minute.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity boundary fan-out: the diff enrolls all recorded PRs from the full session catalog in continuous background polling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Active session chat toolbar resolving dedicated pull-request and issue pills, including workspace-less and cross-repository records
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reference parsing and pill construction are synchronous on the active toolbar render path but linear/small per artifact in normal use. Network refreshes are fire-and-forget; fallback labels/icons render without awaiting them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll GitHub issue details for issue pills
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial REST request per distinct active-session issue when issue pills are visible, then one per open issue every 15 minutes; duplicate model users coalesce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only workspace repository GitHub metadata supplied issue refs; workspace-less and foreign-repository recorded issues remained generic and did not create issue models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by toolbar rendering, so it is off the visual critical path; it consumes background network/API capacity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Recorded artifacts plus repository associations in the active session. Shared model collections coalesce identical GitHub coordinates; artifact storage normally deduplicates identical values.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PR data is supplied by the central poller. When issue pills are enabled, all distinct issue models refresh concurrently and each open issue schedules a 15-minute poll; there is no shared limiter across distinct issues.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Issue models debounce on-demand refreshes for 60 seconds and retain up to 100 disposed snapshots with ETags; warm unchanged responses can be 304. PR references use shared live models. getSessionGitHubReferences itself does not cache but recomputes only when observed session/workspace/artifact inputs invalidate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and request count; lower magnitude than catalog-wide PR polling because only one active session participates and issue polling is much slower.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical active sessions likely contain few issue links, so this active-only, 15-minute fan-out was not separately reported despite the same unbounded artifact input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: dedicated issue resolution adds network work but is active-session-only, off the UI critical path, cached, and has a 15-minute cadence; the stronger catalog-wide PR fan-out is reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host artifact hydration, deduplication, presentation filtering, opening, and removal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hydrated artifact metadata is synchronously partitioned and parsed before pill sections update. Opening uses existing commands. User-initiated removal crosses the existing session-provider removal path and is not required for normal rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove one recorded artifact/reference through the owning sessions provider, which may persist agent-host metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider call per explicit user removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same recorded item was removable from the generic artifact/reference pill through the same management-service path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the removal action waits for it; ordinary hydration and rendering do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The persisted artifact list for one session. Parsing/filtering is linear except merging recorded and associated GitHub references, which can be quadratic in those two lists, but realistic lists are expected to be small and updates are event-driven rather than frame/input driven.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local parsing and deduplication are synchronous. A removal is one user-triggered provider operation; there is no per-item boundary fan-out in this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Artifact observables use structural equality, duplicate artifact values are rejected by SessionArtifactCollection, and derived consumers update only when observed sources change. No new cache with lifecycle risk is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the changed parsing/presentation work is local and that removal preserves the existing one-call boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persisted list sizes are unbounded, but no changed hot loop or newly multiplied persistence/IPC operation was found here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: the presentation and provider changes do not independently add a realistic expensive-boundary regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and surrounding model/provider call paths. One high-confidence network boundary-fanout regression was submitted for catalog-wide polling of every recorded PR; active-toolbar and artifact-provider scenarios did not justify separate findings.
